subject: Add __attribute__((noescape)) on pointers in public API
perf_evidence: Message: 'Add __attribute__((noescape)) on pointers in public API ... Without LTO its the only way to inform the compiler that the pointer does not become globally visible due to the function call.' - lets callers keep values in registers / avoid reloads (codegen intent).
change_summary: Defines XXH_NOESCAPE (__attribute__((noescape)) when supported, i.e. clang) and annotates pointer parameters of the public API declarations/definitions (XXH32/XXH64/XXH3 one-shot, state, canonical functions). No body changes.

units.name: library implementation (XXH_INLINE_ALL; XXH32/XXH64/XXH3/XXH128, XXH32 streaming, hashFromCanonical)
units.evidence: IR identical for all 7 targets after normalization; Alive2 EQUIV both directions (XXH32 len20 (value args), XXH32 stream 10+10 (value args), XXH64 len40, XXH3 len20/200, XXH3_128bits len20, hashFromCanonical)

units.name: separately compiled client: local buffer passed to XXH64 / XXH64_update / XXH3_64bits_update, then an unknown ext() call, then the buffer is re-read
units.evidence: clang emits 'nocapture' on the call arguments/declarations in new (the only IR effect; no downstream optimization appeared in these clients). The Alive2 pin cannot parse 'nocapture', so the shared runner strips it on both sides; Alive2 then reports EQUIV for the 3 targets, but that check no longer contains the change itself

notes: Implementation-level IR is identical (EQUIV). The attribute's effect is a cross-TU contract that becomes LLVM 'nocapture' at call sites/declarations; tools/alive_check.py's normalization removes ' nocapture' (Alive2 cannot parse it), so Alive2 cannot see or check the change: the r_client EQUIV is recorded but only proves the clients equal modulo the stripped attribute -> unit UNSUPPORTED(other). Commit verdict by METHOD aggregation -> UNSUPPORTED; library semantics unchanged.
